-- Trigger function for multi-table audit on Projects
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.tr_Projects_MultiTableAudit_func()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Log to AuditLog
    IF (TG_OP = 'INSERT') THEN
        INSERT INTO public.AuditLog (TableName, Operation, RecordID, NewValues)
        SELECT
            'Projects',
            'INSERT',
            NEW.ProjectID,
            'Name=' || NEW.ProjectName || ', Budget=' || COALESCE(NEW.Budget::TEXT, 'NULL');
        
        -- Update department budget allocation for INSERT
        UPDATE public.Departments d
        SET Budget = d.Budget + COALESCE(NEW.Budget, 0)
        WHERE d.DepartmentID = NEW.DepartmentID;
        
    ELSIF (TG_OP = 'UPDATE') THEN
        INSERT INTO public.AuditLog (TableName, Operation, RecordID, NewValues)
        SELECT
            'Projects',
            'UPDATE',
            NEW.ProjectID,
            'Name=' || NEW.ProjectName || ', Budget=' || COALESCE(NEW.Budget::TEXT, 'NULL');
        
        -- Update department budget allocation for UPDATE
        UPDATE public.Departments d
        SET Budget = d.Budget + COALESCE(NEW.Budget, 0) - COALESCE(OLD.Budget, 0)
        WHERE d.DepartmentID = NEW.DepartmentID;
    END IF;
    
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Create the trigger
CREATE TRIGGER tr_Projects_MultiTableAudit
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON public.Projects
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION public.tr_Projects_MultiTableAudit_func();

-- =============================================================================
-- MULTI-TABLE TRIGGER (affects 2+ tables)
-- Requirement 1.2: multi-table triggers pattern
-- Converted from SQL Server to PostgreSQL
-- =============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.tr_employees_auditandbudget_func()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Handle UPDATE operation
    IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
        -- Write to AuditLog table
        INSERT INTO public.AuditLog (TableName, Operation, RecordID, OldValues, NewValues)
        SELECT
            'Employees',
            'UPDATE',
            new_table.EmployeeID,
            'Salary=' || CAST(old_table.Salary AS VARCHAR(20)),
            'Salary=' || CAST(new_table.Salary AS VARCHAR(20))
        FROM new_table
        INNER JOIN old_table ON new_table.EmployeeID = old_table.EmployeeID;

        -- Update Department budget when salary changes
        UPDATE public.Departments dept
        SET Budget = dept.Budget + (new_table.Salary - old_table.Salary)
        FROM new_table
        INNER JOIN old_table ON new_table.EmployeeID = old_table.EmployeeID
        WHERE dept.DepartmentID = new_table.DepartmentID
          AND new_table.Salary <> old_table.Salary;

    -- Handle INSERT operation
    ELSIF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
        -- Write to AuditLog table
        INSERT INTO public.AuditLog (TableName, Operation, RecordID, NewValues)
        SELECT
            'Employees',
            'INSERT',
            new_table.EmployeeID,
            'Name=' || new_table.FirstName || ' ' || new_table.LastName || ', Salary=' || CAST(new_table.Salary AS VARCHAR(20))
        FROM new_table;

        -- Add salary to department budget
        UPDATE public.Departments dept
        SET Budget = dept.Budget + new_table.Salary
        FROM new_table
        WHERE dept.DepartmentID = new_table.DepartmentID;

    -- Handle DELETE operation
    ELSIF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
        -- Write to AuditLog table
        INSERT INTO public.AuditLog (TableName, Operation, RecordID, OldValues)
        SELECT
            'Employees',
            'DELETE',
            old_table.EmployeeID,
            'Name=' || old_table.FirstName || ' ' || old_table.LastName || ', Salary=' || CAST(old_table.Salary AS VARCHAR(20))
        FROM old_table;

        -- Subtract salary from department budget
        UPDATE public.Departments dept
        SET Budget = dept.Budget - old_table.Salary
        FROM old_table
        WHERE dept.DepartmentID = old_table.DepartmentID;
    END IF;

    -- For AFTER triggers, return value is ignored but required
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
        RETURN OLD;
    ELSE
        RETURN NEW;
    END IF;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Create the trigger binding
CREATE TRIGGER tr_employees_auditandbudget
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.Employees
REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS new_table OLD TABLE AS old_table
FOR EACH STATEMENT
EXECUTE FUNCTION public.tr_employees_auditandbudget_func();

-- =============================================================================
-- SCHEMA: Procedures using table types as parameters
-- =============================================================================

-- Table type equivalent: OrderLineType
-- PostgreSQL doesn't support user-defined table types as parameters.
-- Instead, we'll use a temporary table or a composite type approach.
-- For this conversion, we'll create a composite type to represent a single line,
-- and accept an array of that type.

CREATE TYPE public.order_line_type AS (
    ProductID INT,
    Quantity INT,
    UnitPrice DECIMAL(12, 2)
);

-- 14. Procedure accepting table type parameter (OrderLineType)
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sp_CreateOrderWithLines(
    p_CustomerName VARCHAR(200),
    p_Lines public.order_line_type[]
)
RETURNS TABLE(
    NewOrderID INT,
    TotalAmount DECIMAL(12, 2)
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_OrderID INT;
    v_Total DECIMAL(12, 2);
    v_Line public.order_line_type;
BEGIN
    -- Calculate total from the array parameter
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM((line).Quantity * (line).UnitPrice), 0)
    INTO v_Total
    FROM unnest(p_Lines) AS line;

    -- Insert into Orders table
    INSERT INTO public.Orders (CustomerName, TotalAmount)
    VALUES (p_CustomerName, COALESCE(v_Total, 0))
    RETURNING OrderID INTO v_OrderID;

    -- Insert order lines
    INSERT INTO public.OrderLines (OrderID, ProductID, Quantity, UnitPrice)
    SELECT v_OrderID, (line).ProductID, (line).Quantity, (line).UnitPrice
    FROM unnest(p_Lines) AS line;

    -- Return result set
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT v_OrderID, v_Total;
END;
$$;

        e.LastName,
        e.Salary AS UpdatedSalary
    FROM public.Employees e
    INNER JOIN UNNEST(p_updates) AS u ON e.EmployeeID = u.EmployeeID;
END;
$$;

-- =============================================================================
-- PROCEDURE 8: Another cursor pattern - department report generation
-- Uses cursor to iterate departments and build summary
-- Converted to PostgreSQL - refactored to set-based operation
-- =============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sp_CursorDepartmentReport()
RETURNS TABLE (
    DepartmentName VARCHAR(100),
    EmployeeCount INT,
    TotalSalary DECIMAL(12,2),
    BudgetUtilization DECIMAL(5,2)
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- PostgreSQL best practice: use set-based operation instead of cursor
    -- This is more efficient and idiomatic in PostgreSQL
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        d.DepartmentName::VARCHAR(100),
        COALESCE(emp_stats.EmpCount, 0)::INT,
        COALESCE(emp_stats.TotalSal, 0)::DECIMAL(12,2),
        CASE 
            WHEN d.BudgetAmount > 0 THEN 
                (COALESCE(emp_stats.TotalSal, 0) / d.BudgetAmount * 100)::DECIMAL(5,2)
            ELSE 
                0::DECIMAL(5,2)
        END AS BudgetUtilization
    FROM 
        public.Departments d
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT 
            DepartmentID,
            COUNT(*)::INT AS EmpCount,
            COALESCE(SUM(Salary), 0) AS TotalSal
        FROM 
            public.Employees
        GROUP BY 
            DepartmentID
    ) emp_stats ON d.DepartmentID = emp_stats.DepartmentID
    WHERE 
        d.IsActive = true
    ORDER BY 
        CASE 
            WHEN d.BudgetAmount > 0 THEN 
                (COALESCE(emp_stats.TotalSal, 0) / d.BudgetAmount * 100)
            ELSE 
                0
        END DESC;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.sp_CursorDepartmentReport() IS 'Department report generation - refactored from cursor to set-based operation for better performance';

-- =============================================================================
-- PROCEDURE 3: Multiple result sets from a single procedure
-- Returns employee details, department summary, and processing queue status
-- =============================================================================
-- NOTE: PostgreSQL does not support multiple result sets from a single procedure/function.
-- This has been split into separate functions, one for each result set.
-- Applications must call each function separately.

-- Result Set 1: Employee listing
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sp_MultiResultSetDashboard_Employees(
    p_DepartmentID INT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    EmployeeID INT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Email VARCHAR,
    Salary NUMERIC,
    DepartmentName VARCHAR
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        e.EmployeeID,
        (e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName)::TEXT AS FullName,
        e.Email,
        e.Salary,
        d.DepartmentName
    FROM public.Employees e
    INNER JOIN public.Departments d ON e.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID
    WHERE (p_DepartmentID IS NULL OR e.DepartmentID = p_DepartmentID)
    ORDER BY e.LastName, e.FirstName;
END;
$$;

-- Result Set 2: Department budget summary
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sp_MultiResultSetDashboard_DepartmentSummary(
    p_DepartmentID INT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    DepartmentID INT,
    DepartmentName VARCHAR,
    BudgetAmount NUMERIC,
    HeadCount BIGINT,
    TotalSalary NUMERIC,
    RemainingBudget NUMERIC
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        d.DepartmentID,
        d.DepartmentName,
        d.BudgetAmount,
        COUNT(e.EmployeeID) AS HeadCount,
        COALESCE(SUM(e.Salary), 0) AS TotalSalary,
        d.BudgetAmount - COALESCE(SUM(e.Salary), 0) AS RemainingBudget
    FROM public.Departments d
    LEFT JOIN public.Employees e ON d.DepartmentID = e.DepartmentID
    WHERE (p_DepartmentID IS NULL OR d.DepartmentID = p_DepartmentID)
    GROUP BY d.DepartmentID, d.DepartmentName, d.BudgetAmount;
END;
$$;

-- Result Set 3: Pending processing queue items
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sp_MultiResultSetDashboard_PendingQueue(
    p_DepartmentID INT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    QueueID INT,
    EmployeeName TEXT,
    ActionType VARCHAR,
    Priority INT,
    Status VARCHAR,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        pq.QueueID,
        (e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName)::TEXT AS EmployeeName,
        pq.ActionType,
        pq.Priority,
        pq.Status,
        pq.CreatedAt
    FROM public.ProcessingQueue pq
    INNER JOIN public.Employees e ON pq.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID
    WHERE pq.Status = 'Pending'
      AND (p_DepartmentID IS NULL OR e.DepartmentID = p_DepartmentID)
    ORDER BY pq.Priority ASC, pq.CreatedAt ASC;
END;
$$;

-- Result Set 4: Recent audit trail
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sp_MultiResultSetDashboard_AuditTrail(
    p_DepartmentID INT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    AuditID INT,
    TableName VARCHAR,
    Operation VARCHAR,
    RecordID INT,
    ChangedBy VARCHAR,
    ChangedAt TIMESTAMP
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        al.AuditID,
        al.TableName,
        al.Operation,
        al.RecordID,
        al.ChangedBy,
        al.ChangedAt
    FROM public.AuditLog al
    ORDER BY al.ChangedAt DESC
    LIMIT 10;
END;
$$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.sp_MultiResultSetDashboard_Employees(INT) IS 'Result Set 1 from sp_MultiResultSetDashboard - Employee listing';
COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.sp_MultiResultSetDashboard_DepartmentSummary(INT) IS 'Result Set 2 from sp_MultiResultSetDashboard - Department budget summary';
COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.sp_MultiResultSetDashboard_PendingQueue(INT) IS 'Result Set 3 from sp_MultiResultSetDashboard - Pending processing queue items';
COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.sp_MultiResultSetDashboard_AuditTrail(INT) IS 'Result Set 4 from sp_MultiResultSetDashboard - Recent audit trail (note: does not use DepartmentID parameter)';

-- =============================================================================
-- PROCEDURE 9: Multiple result sets with conditional output
-- Returns different result sets based on parameters
-- =============================================================================
-- Note: PostgreSQL does not support multiple result sets from a single function.
-- This implementation uses a refcursor approach to return multiple result sets.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sp_EmployeeReport(
    p_ReportType VARCHAR(20),
    p_DepartmentID INTEGER DEFAULT NULL,
    OUT ref_header REFCURSOR,
    OUT ref_data REFCURSOR
)
RETURNS RECORD
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Result Set 1: Always returned - report header
    OPEN ref_header FOR
    SELECT
        p_ReportType AS ReportType,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AS GeneratedAt,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM public.Employees) AS TotalEmployees;

    -- Result Set 2: Conditional on report type
    IF p_ReportType = 'SALARY' THEN
        OPEN ref_data FOR
        SELECT
            e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS EmployeeName,
            e.Salary,
            d.DepartmentName,
            RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.DepartmentID ORDER BY e.Salary DESC) AS SalaryRank
        FROM public.Employees e
        INNER JOIN public.Departments d ON e.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID
        WHERE (p_DepartmentID IS NULL OR e.DepartmentID = p_DepartmentID);
    ELSIF p_ReportType = 'HISTORY' THEN
        OPEN ref_data FOR
        SELECT
            e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS EmployeeName,
            sh.OldSalary,
            sh.NewSalary,
            sh.ChangeDate,
            sh.Reason
        FROM public.SalaryHistory sh
        INNER JOIN public.Employees e ON sh.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID
        WHERE (p_DepartmentID IS NULL OR e.DepartmentID = p_DepartmentID)
        ORDER BY sh.ChangeDate DESC;
    ELSE
        OPEN ref_data FOR
        SELECT
            e.EmployeeID,
            e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS EmployeeName,
            e.Email,
            d.DepartmentName,
            e.HireDate
        FROM public.Employees e
        INNER JOIN public.Departments d ON e.DepartmentID = d.DepartmentID
        WHERE (p_DepartmentID IS NULL OR e.DepartmentID = p_DepartmentID);
    END IF;
END;
$$;

-- Converted from SQL Server procedure: sales.sp_GetExternalCustomerData
-- Returns customer data with cross-database reference pattern converted

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sales.sp_GetExternalCustomerData()
RETURNS TABLE (
    CustomerID INTEGER,
    CustomerName TEXT,
    Email TEXT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_sql TEXT;
BEGIN
    -- Cross-database reference pattern using three-part naming
    -- In production this would reference another database on the same server
    -- PostgreSQL uses foreign data wrappers (FDW) or dblink for cross-database access
    v_sql := '
        SELECT CustomerID, CustomerName, Email
        FROM ExternalCRM.public.Customers
        WHERE IsActive = true';

    -- Print the cross-database query for detection purposes
    -- Actual execution would fail without ExternalCRM database or FDW setup
    RAISE NOTICE 'Cross-database reference detected:';
    RAISE NOTICE '%', v_sql;

    -- Return local data as fallback so the procedure produces results
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CustomerName, c.Email
    FROM sales.Customers c;
END;
$$;
